formation.explanation: Append is buffered during prepare, sent locally during Leader/Accept, or forwarded. Current-ballot promises populate participant slots; a prepare quorum selects maximal accepted-round/index history, synchronizes it, then sends AcceptSync. Followers synchronize and acknowledge, and incremental appends use sequence validation. Current-ballot Accepted messages update leader indexes; a write quorum causes decided-index advancement and decision propagation. Read APIs expose the decided prefix for application use. Storage load reconstructs accepted extent and reads classify entries against the decided boundary. The optional actor tracks a client EntryId to an assigned end index and ballot; on ticks it resolves success using decided index before testing ballot supersession. Ordered consumption also includes subscriptions: compacted-prefix reads contain a single summary marker, while runtime subscription cursors currently advance once per emitted representation.

context.explanation: Tick drives BLE; matching heartbeat rounds/configurations influence leader selection. SequencePaxos requires a higher ballot before initiating preparation. Followers persist a higher promise, reject lower-ballot replication and accept same-ballot prepare only during recovery. Reconnect and sequence gaps can initiate equal-ballot recovery. StopSign seals the old log and delegates startup/state transfer of a new configuration to the caller. Construction reads the stored promise into protocol and BLE recovery context, while cached accepted metadata comes from the backend. The actor serializes incoming messages and commands but runs completion processing only on tick branches.

connection.explanation: Authority alone does not enable acceptance: the new leader first gathers promise support and adopts accepted history, including prior decisions, before appending buffered work. A stopped selected history blocks appends. Followers require the promised ballot and appropriate phase; incremental old-session work is rejected or triggers recovery. Equal-ballot recovery resets phase and sequence before synchronization, leaving a specific delayed-AcceptSync history question. Client assignment records survive incoming higher-ballot synchronization until a later notifier drain. Whether the assigned entry survives depends on adopted history, rather than on numeric decided-index advancement alone. For the already read runtime consumer, stored assignment alone does not imply entry preservation: core synchronization can replace unchosen history while Pending.assigned stays unchanged, and the notifier numeric-success arm precedes supersession.

items.rationale:
Requirement and applicability: claim-notify-correspondence v1 is a success-only implication derived from append_notify promising the submitted entry's decided index. The Superseded documentation permits conservative failure when an entry might survive leadership change; it does not permit success for a different value. The fixed check uses unique submitted payload 101 and replacement payload 202, no batching, compaction, crashes or storage failures. Entry and snapshot types instantiate the public API; TestRuntime supplies ordinary Tokio spawn/sleep matching the repository adapter, without intercepting protocol state.

Legal history and producer reachability: the fixed source builds three valid fresh instances, establishes leader 1 through generated Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync traffic, checks all accepted and decided extents are zero, then moves the live node into spawn_actor. The original future is created by one actual append_notify(101). Its two actual AcceptDecide messages are observed and dropped during node-1 isolation; independent reads confirm peers 2 and 3 have no accepted entries. Node 2 uses public manual leadership and obtains node 3's promise before accepting replacement 202. The new quorum does not contain the original entry, so replacing its unchosen position is legal. Deferred Prepare and subsequent Promise/AcceptSync are delivered as generated, preserving retained per-link order; no incoming payload or storage state is manufactured. Core peers are driven within a finite prefix, and no liveness/deadline property is inferred from their tick frequency. No reconnect injection or duplicate delivery is required.

Observed prefix and result: execution adcc1c901782418b971256e7f414647b contains admission event 22 with payload 101, origin_decided 0 and empty peers; event 31 follows actual round-2 quorum work and reports replacement 202 decided at end index 1; event 36 follows actual round-2 synchronization and a live actor read showing Decided(202), with the original call still pending. Event 38 records the awaited original future returning success=true, returned_index=1, and a post-completion public read reporting decided_value=202. The monitor matched all three prerequisites and found no parse errors or missing observations. Static prerequisite values are emitted only after assertions against actual messages and reads. The outcome is not inferred from process PASS.

Oracle and correlation: one operation label independently identifies this sole append_notify call and its awaited JoinHandle/oneshot result. No compared value or changing ballot is used as an identity filter. The admission alias is explicitly admission; the assertion compares the actual decided_value with admission.payload only when observed success is true. The returned value is an exclusive accepted end index because append_tracked records get_accepted_idx; reading suffix(k-1) therefore observes the corresponding log entry. For this witness k=1, the live public read contains Decided(202), so neither missing-read sentinel nor zero-index fallback contributes to the comparison. These observations all belong to the same live objects and schedule; there are no isolated producer fragments.

Mechanism and alternatives: incoming higher-ballot handling replaces the old unchosen log and updates decided metadata while the pending assignment remains recorded. run invokes drain_notifiers on a later tick. Its first match arm returns Ok for idx <= decided without checking the stored ballot; the later Superseded arm is bypassed. Quorum preservation protects already-selected history but did not require retaining a value held only by isolated node 1. An earlier notifier tick could return Superseded, which is allowed; the observed pending marker and later success establish the actual timing for this execution. Event and transport channels are drained, real timers run, and teardown follows observation. The test ends after the operation result and independent read, without requiring any conflicting cluster decision.

items.rationale:
The accepted claim-stream-order v1 follows the public subscribe_decided contract: backlog and later LogEntry output must be in log order. The selected oracle only forbids a decrease in original position among retained Decided entries. It allows equal positions and ignores snapshot markers, so it does not invent an exactly-once contract or demand recovery of compacted individual entries.

The fixed harness establishes a valid three-node configuration and generates every protocol message through actual core instances. It uses public manual leadership, appends five unique values, and requires all replicas to report decided extent 5 before compaction. A public precompaction read records original history [81,23,67,42,19]. snapshot(Some(3),true) executes the real compaction producer with a prefix-preserving Snapshot implementation; reads confirm summary boundary 3 followed by retained values 42 and 19. The original actor core is moved into spawn_actor with no storage replacement or private mutation. The public constructor does not require empty history. The sole subscription is below configured capacity, its command precedes a same-channel read barrier, and the receiver is actively drained. Events and outgoing transport are also drained; ordinary real Tokio timers drive the actor.

Execution 09941e2a9e084150bd1c84ff412dd312 records the declared admission for subscription from-zero with from=0, compacted=3, decided=5 and two retained entries. It then records a snapshot marker followed by Decided values 42,19,42,19, at independently recovered positions 3,4,3,4. The completed stream_window event has order_preserved=false and observed_items=5. Final live actor reads verify the stable retained suffix is still [42,19] at extent 5. No additional appends, reconfiguration, recovery, leadership changes or compaction occur during the observation. This is one legal history with the actual compaction producer, actual cursor consumer and actual subscriber endpoint.

The operation identity is the unique subscription label, independent of payloads and the compared order result. Each Decided payload is mapped to its unique rank in the separately observed original log; deliberately nonmonotonic payload numbers prevent confusing numeric value order with log order. The source computes order_preserved by checking adjacent ranks for nondecrease. Raw per-item events independently show the decisive 4-to-3 decrease. The result is not predetermined by the input or selected by an observed failure. Initial catch-up values are observed rather than asserted to match the expected stream order; the observation ends at a fixed elapsed-time cutoff regardless of reversal.

The implementation explanation is conditional and matches this prefix. Initial push_to_sub successfully emits three representations: one snapshot and two retained entries. Its cursor increments from 0 to 3 rather than advancing to original extent 5. A later push_to_all_subs therefore reads original positions 3 and 4 again and appends them after the already delivered position 4. Ordinary noncompacted reads do not exhibit this representation/position mismatch. Channel-full and closure branches do not explain the witness: capacity is 32 and only five observed items are emitted to an actively drained receiver. The finite window is sufficient for a positive safety counterexample; no deadline failure or infinite-stall conclusion is inferred. The process completed and all result data exists; process PASS alone is not the evidence.
